core_obligations: Record the easy case: if the morphism restricts to a closed immersion on every integral closed subscheme of the source, then the identity holds by the definition of capping with a first Chern class (proof lines 4644-4648).

Reduce to a disjoint union: write the cycle as a finite combination of distinct integral closed subschemes, let the W'_i be their images, and form the diagram of disjoint unions; since the family of components is locally finite and the morphism is proper, the images form a locally finite family and all the morphisms in the diagram are proper; the cycle may be viewed on the disjoint union of the components, and the opening remark applies to the two horizontal morphisms, so it suffices to prove the identity for the induced morphism between the disjoint unions (proof lines 4650-4673).

Finish: the reduced situation means one may assume the source and target integral, the morphism dominant and the cycle the fundamental class, in which case the identity is the statement that the two descriptions of the first Chern class agree as cycles (proof lines 4674-4677).
proof_roadmap: The closed immersion case by definition (proof lines 4644-4648).
Reduce to the induced morphism between the disjoint unions of the components and of their images (proof lines 4650-4673).
Apply the equality of first Chern classes as cycles (proof lines 4674-4677).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the projection formula for a first Chern class against a proper pushforward: pushing forward the cap of the pullback of an invertible sheaf equals capping the pushforward with the Chern class of that sheaf (statement lines 4630-4642, tag 02SU). The proof first isolates the case where the morphism restricts to closed immersions on integral subschemes, then reduces the general case by forming the disjoint unions of the components of the cycle and of their images and observing that the identity on those two disjoint unions implies it for the original morphism, and finally reduces to an integral dominant morphism. The reduction through the disjoint unions is the substance, so the claim is H2.
